name: dsh-raven-research
description: DeepSeek Harness plugin for progressive, source-grounded deep research, writing, and learning: steerable checkpoints and citations verified against retrieved sources
dshComment: No 'bundle' key on purpose, and its absence is the isolation guarantee.
Declaring 'dsh.bundle.patch' is what makes 'dsh plugin add' append this package to a
profile's 'dsh.profile.bundles', which would apply cordis.patch.yml and give Raven a
host-plane row. That row registers the settings namespace, and a settings page is
global: a user in any other mode would see a Raven card. It also decides the browser
half, because the web app loads a package's client bundle only when the composition
carries a row naming that package.
So installing this package contributes nothing until a session is started in Raven
mode. cordis.patch.yml is still shipped, as an opt-in overlay for a deployment that
wants the card and accepts losing isolation; see the comments in that file.

scripts.lint: oxlint --deny-warnings src tests scripts tsdown.config.ts vitest.config.ts
scripts.check: pnpm run lint && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run build && pnpm run test
scripts.check:release: pnpm run check && pnpm run test:pack && pnpm run test:dsh

peerDependenciesComment: Every peer is '*' on purpose, and it is not laziness about ranges.
A profile installs plugins with autoInstallPeers:false and nodeLinker:hoisted precisely so an
out-of-tree plugin's peers fall through to the RUNNING Harness installation and every plugin
shares ONE cordis instance. A narrowed range cannot make a mismatched deployment work: it makes
the install fail, or resolves a second copy whose services the Harness cannot see -- a failure
that looks like an absent service rather than a version conflict. So the range is not where
The 'dshRaven' block at the bottom of this file is. It names the exact Harness version and commit
this build was tested against, scripts/verify-dsh.ts is the executable check of it, and the
release workflow refuses to publish without it. Read the pin, not the ranges, to know what runs.
Consequence to accept: a pre-1.0 prerelease that reshapes a seam gives NO install-time signal here. The
pin plus 'pnpm run test:dsh' against a matching checkout is the only thing that catches it, which
is why that gate is mandatory before a release. See README.md, 'Version pinning and peer dependencies'.
